title: Wednesday's page
how: Everything here passed my check and a blind reviewer's for obvious faults; the reviewer's remaining notes are beside each. Pick one per item; a note is optional. Your picks save on the page.

New today: how Sheila looks at you as you walk past her, three ways; and nine pieces of 1990 street clutter, each against photographs of the real thing (the tenth, the street name plate, waits on a font). The rest is Tuesday's, not yet picked.
Faces: front and profile in a plain studio light, and the face speaking a line.
foot: Anything you do not pick carries onto the next page.

sections.name: Sheila, as you walk past her: three ways
sections.note: The same walk three times, filmed in the game. What she has heard of your night changes how she looks at you: knowing nothing, a stranger's glance that lands about ten metres off, lasts half a second and is gone before you are close; half-remembering a story, the same glance and then a second, longer look as you pass; sure it is you, she keeps you in view, says one line, and looks back after you until you are well past. Her voice is not in these (it waits on your paid-voice decision), so her lips do not move; the line is a subtitle. The blind reviewer's remaining notes: her hair and clothes are the game's stand-in, not her casting sheet's (a short greying set, a cardigan and skirt, tinted glasses), so she reads nearer 40 than 53; at the closest moments her eyes are cast steeply down; the look back turns her head but not her shoulders, so it reads as watching where you went more than looking over her shoulder; the first glance barely shows from this camera, as she already faces that way; you are in the picture for only about two of the 24 seconds; and three single frames are missing (a tenth of a second each, not visible).

pictures.alt: She is sure it is you

sections.name: Street clutter: The pillar box
sections.note: The Post Office cipher and lettering are left off until you choose the postal service's mark (canon: every brand is fictional). Reviewer's notes: the cap's beads are small and round where the real ones are bolder; the cap reads a little like a disc; the collection tablet is a plain white block; the black base is a touch glossy. Three views: front, three-quarter, side; the grey figure is 1.80 m.

pictures.alt: The pillar box: front, three-quarter and side

sections.name: Street clutter: The telephone kiosk (KX100, 1985 livery)
sections.note: The telephone company's mark is left off until you name it. Reviewer's notes (passed only just): the foot shows two dark plates where the real one is open to the pavement from about 10 cm; the bands on the sides are deep; the payphone is plain. Three views: front, three-quarter, side; the grey figure is 1.80 m.

pictures.alt: The telephone kiosk (KX100, 1985 livery): front, three-quarter and side

sections.name: Street clutter: The Belisha beacon (one of the pair)
sections.note: Reviewer's notes: the white band under the collar is short; a small cap on the globe. Three views: front, three-quarter, side; the grey figure is 1.80 m.

pictures.alt: The Belisha beacon (one of the pair): front, three-quarter and side

sections.name: Street clutter: The bus stop
sections.note: The plain official sign, not a bus company's flag. Reviewer's notes: 'Bus Stop' is smaller and lighter than on the real sign; the bus picture is simpler; the border thin. Three views: front, three-quarter, side; the grey figure is 1.80 m.

pictures.alt: The bus stop: front, three-quarter and side

sections.name: Street clutter: The dustbin (the yard)
sections.note: No free photograph of a 1990 bin was found, so it is made from a 90 litre bin's measurements. Reviewer's notes: it reads more like polished aluminium than dull zinc; the ribs are broad bands; the lid's handle is thin from the side. Three views: front, three-quarter, side; the grey figure is 1.80 m.

pictures.alt: The dustbin (the yard): front, three-quarter and side

sections.name: Street clutter: The bollard
sections.note: After the listed cast-iron cannon-and-ball bollards of Leeds, about 0.75 m. Reviewer's notes: no neck under the ball; a slim shaft; very clean paint. Three views: front, three-quarter, side; the grey figure is 1.80 m.

pictures.alt: The bollard: front, three-quarter and side

sections.name: Street clutter: The telegraph pole
sections.note: The street will run its wires to the houses. Reviewer's notes: no distribution box under the ring at the top; the wire stubs slope down too steeply; an even warm brown where real poles weather to grey-brown. Three views: front, three-quarter, side; the grey figure is 1.80 m.

pictures.alt: The telegraph pole: front, three-quarter and side

sections.name: Street clutter: The grit bin
sections.note: Whether glass-fibre bins had replaced concrete ones by 1990 is uncertain. Reviewer's notes: the lid is a flat slab; the edges are sharp; the yellow is spotless. Three views: front, three-quarter, side; the grey figure is 1.80 m.

pictures.alt: The grit bin: front, three-quarter and side

sections.name: Street clutter: The litter bin
sections.note: The usual 1990 type is uncertain; this is an open-top bin on a post. Reviewer's notes: a few pixels of jagged shadow under the rim; a glossy highlight; the letters slightly uneven. Three views: front, three-quarter, side; the grey figure is 1.80 m.

pictures.alt: The litter bin: front, three-quarter and side

sections.name: Ron, threatening: two ways of making his voice act
sections.note: The same line in Ron's voice, made two different ways, heard blind (which is which is kept off the page). Both passed the accent, words and likeness checks and a blind reviewer. Which sounds more like Ron meaning it? Only Ron's threat is here tonight: his other lines, and Sheila's and Darren's, failed the accent check in one way or the other.
sections.line: Walk away, son. Thirty years on the docks, and I never once had to ask a man twice.

sections.name: Sheila Dunn
sections.note: Her fifth face, shaped to the concept portrait by measurement. The blind reviewer's remaining notes: she reads about 45 to 48, not 53 (smooth forehead and upper lip, no smoker's lines); a peach tint on the upper lids and red inner corners; the hair darker and warmer than the concept's ash grey-brown; the proportions close to the concept. In the speaking frames her eyes blur during a blink. The haircut is Epic's nearest, not yet a set; her glasses come with her clothes.

sections.name: Darren Milner
sections.note: His fifth face, shaped to the concept portrait by measurement. The blind reviewer's remaining notes: the lids cut into the iris and the brows are heavy, so he looks sullen rather than quick and amused, and about 30; orange upper lids and red inner corners; the brown of the hair darker and redder than the concept's, the blond a band at the ends. The haircut is Epic's nearest, not yet a grown-out perm.

sections.name: The conversation light
sections.note: A faint light on whoever you are talking to, from above and to one side, and a catch-light in the eyes. It lights only their skin (not their hair), only that person, costs 0.2 ms a frame, and fades six seconds after they stop; a face already in sun gets none. Shown on Ron: judge the light, not the face.

pictures.alt: Ron in the street's daylight, no conversation light
The same moment and camera, with the conversation light

sections.name: Ron's voice, in the game
sections.note: His July voice, as the game speaks it. Carried from 25 September.
sections.line: Forty years on the docks and they finished it with a letter. Mickey gave me the door. I don't forget that.

sections.name: Darren's voice, in the game
sections.note: His approved voice (Scottish, which the sheet notes), as the game speaks it. Carried from 25 September.
sections.line: A shape's not much to go on. Half the town could pass for that on a night like this.

sections.name: Ron, while he thinks
sections.note: When you ask him something, he says one of these at once, in his own voice, and stops the moment his answer starts. It covers the wait; there is no loading sign. Both of his, one after the other.

sections.name: Darren, while he thinks
sections.note: The same for Darren. Sheila has none yet: both tries leaned away from her accent.
sections.line: Hmm, well now.  /  Let me think.
